author: amitisinvesting
text: This narrative that Palantir $PLTR and Robinhood $HOOD are meme stocks is absolute nonsense and needs to stop. Memestocks are companies that are being hyped up by investors that have zero fundamental reason to gain their appreciation in value. While it can be subjective over how to think of what constitutes a meme, the idea of comparing the company that deploys software on the battlefield to defend the warfighter or the company that has increased their assets under custody to 1/4th of a TRILLION in less than a year is just ridiculous. Palantir and Robinhood are led by two exceptional founders. Both have executed at a level that has realistically not been seen in the public markets EVER and cultivated an audience of retail investors that saw the potential, believed in them when the world didn't, and continue to see their growth trajectories as exponential. Now, you can absolutely disagree with the market's valuation of these two companies. I think that is a reasonable debate. However, to categorize their aggressive premiums as just filled with memes COMPLETELY discounts why the street is willing to pay a multiple and if you're best argument is valuation, please tell me why $COST Costco deserves a 50 P/E or why $NFLX Netflix, as incredible as it is, deserves to have a premium that is more than triple of $GOOGLon a P/E basis. The point is valuations are debatable but what is not debatable is the level of focus, dedication, and execution $PLTR and $HOOD have shown the public markets. Discounting them as memestocks just makes it seem like you'd rather ignore their execution vs. understand why the markets have given them their multiples.

text: The only problem with all these high flying names gapping up 20% in a day… outside of potential froth in the market which is inventible…. is that it might make you feel that you need to chase and be in every high flying stock. From someone who used to chase aggressively, it just might not be worth it. If you actually understand TA, entry/exits, timing, etc. then chasing is an art that is fueled by momentum and can make you very rich. But if you are like most people that want to beat the S&P by picking stocks, then you are likely trying to find undervalued names that have a minimum of 2 years, likely closer to 5, in order for your thesis to play out. All the people who were in $OSCR went through the pain of it being stuck in range for a while before it had the +20% day that it had today. I’ve personally been through it with $PLTR and $HOOD consolidating for a LONG time before they had their run and changed my life. I couldn’t imagine leaving the story early because I needed to chase another name that was outperforming. That doesn’t mean if you are stuck in an underperforming stock that it will be a winner, it very much could be smart to dump it and move on, but if your conviction (this is where you learn if you have any) is deep and you believe in a name that isn’t running compared to the high flyers, it can be incredibly toxic to leave it and chase something simply because you see it going up. Congrats to everyone in some of these big names that have run like $OSCR $CRCL etc but also just super important to protect your mental if you aren’t in these names and trust in your own thesis for the names you are in — you may be right, may be wrong, but the game is more fun when you see the thesis play out! And if you are right, victory tastes so much sweeter when you go through the adversity of believing when no one did 🚀

text: CANTOR FITZGERALD WEIGHS IN ON RECENT $INTC & $TSM DEVELOPMENTS, SAYS TSMC THE REAL WINNER, BUT RAISES INTEL PT TO $29 FROM $22: "The situation at Intel is extraordinarily complex, but we believe reports suggesting a split of DesignCo/IFS are credible. While still early in the process, all signs indicate that the new administration is pushing this forward. We expect TSMC to participate under specific conditions that are beneficial to them, making TSMC the clear strategic winner. Key Takeaways: • TSMC Will Not License IP to Intel: Any agreement between TSMC and Intel will not include cross-licensing of TSMC’s technology, nor do we see TSMC acquiring IFS. TSMC will not relinquish control of its assets. • Possible Agreement - Leading-Edge Capacity in the U.S. Controlled by TSMC: TSMC is already planning significant capacity expansion in the U.S. and may be willing to run a fab for Intel, as it had previously agreed to do in 2021 before Intel’s leadership change. However, TSMC prefers giga-fabs (250k/wspm) rather than Intel’s smaller fabs (45-60k/wspm), making negotiations complex. • Most Likely Scenario - A U.S. Version of ESMC: We expect a joint venture similar to TSMC’s European Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (ESMC), with TSMC retaining majority control (at least 51%). Funding could come from the U.S. government and major U.S. fabless players like Apple, NVIDIA, AMD, and Qualcomm. • Intel’s Future - BOD Focused on Shareholder Value: With the administration concerned about Intel’s leadership vacuum and financial struggles, we see a higher probability of an Intel DesignCo/IFS split. The most logical operator of IFS is TSMC. Key market implications: 1. TSMC as the clear strategic winner, solidifying its position as the sole leading-edge foundry provider worldwide, reducing tariff concerns. 2. Intel as a tactical long, with its Board focused on maximizing shareholder value. Our revised valuation assigns $25B to IFS, raising our price target to $29 from $22. 3. A single leading-edge fab setup presents a mixed outcome for Semiconductor Capital Equipment (Semi Cap) players, though wafer fab equipment (WFE) demand could rise in 2026. 4. Fabless chipmakers may absorb higher wafer costs for the benefit of geopolitical supply chain stability. 5. Potential U.S. investment in advanced packaging would be an incremental positive for COWOS players ( $AMAT, $LRCX, $ONTO, $CAMT, $NVMI). 6. A modest negative for $AMD, as Intel can now refocus on its x86 product business.

text: HERE’S WHAT ANALYSTS HAVE TO SAY AFTER $AMZN Q1 EARNINGS: Morgan Stanley (Overweight, PT: $250) "We remain confident AMZN will emerge stronger after this period and that its logistics leadership and GenAI-enabled advances will position it for even more (and more profitable) multi-year retail share gains. But, for now, 2H:25 and '26 visibility on the cost to deliver a leading experience for buyers and sellers remains low. [...] Our PT rises 2% to $250 (~35X '26 EPS), and we remain OW as we look for visibility on China tariffs as a catalyst for estimate revisions. Until then, we view AMZN as largely range bound, trading ~$150-$200." Bank of America (Buy, PT: $230) "Amazon has 'material' 3P seller revenue exposure to China and other imports, and AWS lost some ground to Azure in 1Q. [...] AWS is not seeing the benefit of ChatGPT usage like Azure, corporate spend remains steady [...] AWS growth could potentially accelerate in 2H as capacity ramps up. [...] We are raising our PO to $230 from $225 on higher estimates and stable SOP multiples." Evercore ISI (Outperform, PT: $260) "Shares traded off modestly on the soft Q2 Op Income guide and the lack of AWS acceleration given very strong Azure results, but we view the core near-term and long-term thesis as well intact. [...] AWS revenue growth remained consistent at 17% Y/Y, and backlog growth accelerated to 20% Y/Y – a good sign. [...] RH Operating Margins in every segment reflects ongoing and sustainable cost efficiencies." Goldman Sachs (Buy, PT: $220) "Q1 results slightly above the high-end of the guide across revenue and Operating Income [...] AWS revenue growth of +17% YoY was better than feared in Q1 and AMZN once again framed an expectation that the addition of new capacity in 2H25 will support AWS revenue growth. [...] We remain constructive [...] Amazon can produce a solid mix of compounded revenue growth and operating margin expansion." Stifel (Buy, PT: $245) "1Q headline results were better but AWS was marginally below expectations. [...] AWS growth was marginally light, but the forward commentary remains positive (capacity being consumed the moment it becomes available), and backlog growth accelerated by ~600bps. [...] Overall, we remain positive on AMZN, and only slightly revise our forward estimates." Cantor Fitzgerald (Overweight, PT: $240) "AWS margins expanded 250bps Q/Q to 39.5% - the highest levels on record. [...] Despite near-term uncertainties, our long-term thesis on AMZN is intact - AMZN stands to gain the most competitively during macro disruptions in both AWS and Retail businesses over the long term." HSBC (Buy, PT: $240) "We continue to see AMZN as exceptionally well placed and exposed to all the right structural themes. [...] AWS matters above all else (AWS is still 70% of our DCF-based SOTP value for AMZN). [...] We still see implied upside of 26% to our revised USD240 TP." JMP Securities (Market Outperform, PT: $250) "AWS OIM came in well above expectations. [...] AMZN's advertising business remained robust. [...] Management noted demand remains strong and growth would have been higher if not for capacity constraints which are expected to ease in 2H25." BofA Securities (Buy, PT: $230) "AWS lost some ground to Azure [...] Cloud growth can be lumpy [...] AWS growth could potentially accelerate in 2H as capacity ramps up. [...] We are raising our PO to $230 from $225." Susquehanna (Positive, PT: $225) "AMZN's 1Q was generally solid [...] AWS growth was 17% y/y ex-FX [...] We continue to view AMZN as a long-term secular grower underpinned by its strong eCommerce, cloud/AI, and advertising businesses." Piper Sandler "AMZN remains relentless on lowering cost to serve and appears on the cusp of an AI product cycle, although macro creates uncertainty." Wells Fargo (Equal Weight, PT: $201) Rosenblatt (Buy, PT: $288) Wedbush (Outperform, PT: $235)

text: APPLE IS CHANGING THE WAY IT TRAINS ITS AI TO TRY AND CATCH UP Apple $AAPL will begin analyzing data on customers’ devices in a bid to improve its AI platform, a move designed to safeguard user information while still helping it catch up with AI rivals. Apple today typically trains AI models using synthetic data — information that’s meant to mimic real-world inputs without any personal details. The technology works like this: It takes the synthetic data that Apple has created and compares it to a recent sample of user emails within the iPhone, iPad and Mac email app. By using actual emails to check the fake inputs, Apple can then determine which items within its synthetic dataset are most in line with real-world messages. (Source Bloomberg's @markgurman)

text: Canaccord Genuity Raises $AMZN PT to $280 from $265, Maintains Buy, Cites Strong Q4, AI-Led Growth, and Delivery Expansion "Amazon reported solid Q4 results, with total revenue essentially in line with consensus while operating income was decidedly above expectations. Online and Physical Stores revenue were also both ahead of expectations, with unit growth outpacing revenue growth and new brands onboarding, including Clinique, Estée Lauder, Oura Rings, and Armani Beauty. Amazon continues to make major advances in delivery, growing same-day delivery sites by 60% in 2024 and serving over 140 metro areas. Per-unit transportation costs are declining as greater unit availability hits more distribution points, and more items are being included in each delivered package. Amazon also grew its Advertising business 18% during the quarter, and AWS growth of 19% was on par with Q3 levels despite a modestly more difficult comparison. Q1 revenue guidance was a bit light, with the midpoint of the range ~2% below consensus, while operating income guidance was ~14% below expectations at the midpoint, partially reflecting faster depreciation of technology that is becoming outdated more quickly, particularly in the AI sphere. CapEx was $26B during the quarter, and this run rate is expected to continue into 2025, driven by AI investments to stay ahead of growing demand." Analyst: Maria Ripps

A step function increase in data center costs offset the benefits from topline leverage, resulting in incremental EBITDA margin of 78%, in line with prior indications. We increasingly view Uber as a super app with multiple reasons to utilize the product, which includes getting yourself from point A to point B, ordering dinner from local restaurants, and having groceries delivered to your door (with some ads seen along the way). Can Uber continue to execute against the 3-year financial targets established in early 2024 (2024-2026)? Yes, we think Uber will be able to meet or exceed the financial targets outlined in February 2024 (mid-to-high-teens FXN Gross Bookings growth, a high 30% to 40% EBITDA CAGR and 90%+ EBITDA to FCF conversion). The company has executed well since outlining these initial targets, with 21% Gross Bookings growth (FXN), 60% EBITDA growth, and 106% FCF conversion in 2024. We look for GB growth of 16% in each of 2025/2026 driven by continued expansion into non-urban areas (and international expansion) with continued Uber One adoption leading to increased frequency, paired with affordability initiatives. We’re currently modeling EBITDA growth ahead of Gross Bookings and Revenue growth in 2025 and 2026, with leverage spread across G&A and Operations and Support. Will Uber be successful in Delivery and Advertising? We believe Uber will ultimately be successful in Delivery, which also aids in customer acquisition, particularly in less dense/non-urban areas, and view initiatives such as Uber One and increased supply as a major driver of Delivery bookings over time. We are also bullish on the greater retail media sub-segment of digital ads, and Uber has several advantages. Specifically, we view Uber’s location data as a significant data advantage, which is likely to be a source of interest for both national and local businesses, and Uber’s user base is certainly at scale. We view Uber’s low advertising penetration (we believe ~0.9% of core GBs) as an opportunity, given mature retail media products can scale to 5%+ of GMV (or GBs in this case); just getting halfway there, to 2.5% of core GBs (with zero GB growth), would add an incremental >$1bn of annualized revenue." Can Uber continue to execute against the 3-year financial targets established in early 2024 (2024-2026)? Yes, we think Uber will be able to meet or exceed the financial targets outlined in February 2024 (mid-to-high-teens FXN Gross Bookings growth, a high 30% to 40% EBITDA CAGR and 90%+ EBITDA to FCF conversion). The company has executed well since outlining these initial targets, with 21% Gross Bookings growth (FXN), 60% EBITDA growth, and 106% FCF conversion in 2024. We look for GB growth of 16% in each of 2025/2026 driven by continued expansion into non-urban areas (and international expansion) with continued Uber One adoption leading to increased frequency, paired with affordability initiatives. We’re currently modeling EBITDA growth ahead of Gross Bookings and Revenue growth in 2025 and 2026, with leverage spread across G&A and Operations and Support. Will Uber be successful in Delivery and Advertising? We believe Uber will ultimately be successful in Delivery, which also aids in customer acquisition, particularly in less dense/non-urban areas, and view initiatives such as Uber One and increased supply as a major driver of Delivery bookings over time. We are also bullish on the greater retail media sub-segment of digital ads, and Uber has several advantages. Specifically, we view Uber’s location data as a significant data advantage, which is likely to be a source of interest for both national and local businesses, and Uber’s user base is certainly at scale. We view Uber’s low advertising penetration (we believe ~0.9% of core GBs) as an opportunity, given mature retail media products can scale to 5%+ of GMV (or GBs in this case); just getting halfway there, to 2.5% of core GBs (with zero GB growth), would add an incremental >$1bn of annualized revenue." The catalyst is Alibaba's FY3Q25 results on Thursday, February 20, where it could potentially comment on its future capital expenditure plans and the outlook on its public cloud revenue. Alibaba is GDS's largest customer in China and thus has significant implications for its growth outlook. Additionally, if Alibaba signals an increase in AI-related investment—particularly after its recent AI partnership with Apple, a series of Qwen model releases, and ByteDance's aggressive investment plan—this could further boost new order expectations for the entire data center industry. Potential outcomes and implications: Scenario 1: Stable capex. Alibaba signals a flat capex plan in FY26 versus FY25 (~RMB 70 billion total capex) or offers no comment on capex. Cloud revenue outlook remains at a low teens level. Stock impact: No change. Scenario 2: Rising AI investment. Alibaba signals a meaningful upward revision in FY26 capex driven by AI investment (>10% capex raise) and turns more bullish on public cloud revenue growth outlook. Stock impact: We expect more new bookings and faster move-ins for GDS, resulting in a 10% increase in share price. Scenario 3: Capex cut. Alibaba signals a capex decline in the future following relatively high investment in FY25. Stock impact: We expect a slowdown in move-ins, resulting in a 10% decline in share price." Analyst: Yang Liu

text: Barclays Upgrades $VSCO to Overweight from Equalweight, Raises PT to $53 from $51 Analyst comments: "In FY4Q24, VSCO inflected on our proprietary promotional tracker to 'Better,' suggesting improved full-price selling, which will fuel further gross margin expansion. As such, we upgrade shares of VSCO to Overweight from Equalweight. The promo inflection is the final one of the three critical fundamental catalysts that we track: 1) positive promotional inflection (this quarter); 2) positive comp inflection in FY3Q24; and 3) positive sales-to-inventory spread in FY4Q23. While we missed the stock move off its mid-2024 lows, we now have greater confidence in meaningful top-line acceleration and operating margin expansion. We believe consensus estimates are too low and will be revised upwards over the next 12 to 24 months. And where estimates go, the stock should follow." Analyst: Adrienne Yih

text: $PLTR alright folks superbowl coming up after the bell regardless of what happens to the stock, being part of this community and getting to cover Palantir's journey has been one of the greatest blessings in my life. i really can't express my gratitude for people trusting me as a source for their Palantir news and coverage. it's been 4 years, 2k videos, 200 episodes of a weekly Palantir podcast...and I wouldn't have changed a single thing. having said that, we've got a ton of storylines going into earnings that can affect the stock: - is the SARs expense priced in or not? how bad is the hit? - does Palantir need to guide upwards of 35% YoY growth in 2025 for the street to be happy given the multiple its trading at or can they be at 30% and below? - if topline growth isn't as strong, are FCF growth, operating income margins, rule of 40, etc. enough to allow the street to feel Palantir will continue to grow into their potential? - if DeepSeek proved that LLMs are commodities and an LLM company like OpenAI is about to raise at $340B, what does that mean for a company like Palantir that's profitable and growing in the public markets? - what does government growth look like now with DOGE and can Palantir guide for some type of catalyst because of the government's willingness to spend more on software? Overall, I think Dr. Karp, Shaym Sankar and the entire team are going to crush it by essentially making the same argument they have made for 2 years: Palantir creates outcomes and that is what their customers pay for, not LLMs that can be found a dime-a-dozen and simply plugged into AIP, which is the software layered on Foundry that Palantir believes can create such incredible and transformative use cases (and we've seen many case studies of this already) that lead to them becoming one of the most important companies in the world. The stock will likely see algos and headlines that can move it, but this quarter is going to be determined by guidance, their ability to show continued growth and the market's overall interpretation of where Palantir lies in the broader AI sector. TIME TO EMBRACE ANOTHER CHAPTER IN THE ONGOING STORY OF ONE OF THE MOST EXCITING COMPANIES ON PLANET EARTH. & the best part is, we get to all embrace that chapter together, as a community. LFG.

text: Guggenheim and Goldman Sachs both weighed in after Senate changes to the House IRA bill sent solar stocks sliding. Guggenheim says residential solar looks badly hit—especially for names like $RUN, $ENPH, and $SEDG—as the bill phases out tax credits for leasing models starting 2026. Hedge funds called the outlook “dead” for resi, with one saying ENPH may need major opex cuts just to stay profitable. On the other hand, Guggenheim and Goldman both say utility-scale players like $FSLR, $NXT, and $ARRY are in far better shape. The 45X manufacturing credits remain largely intact through 2031, with strong safe harbor protections. Goldman notes the outcome is “relatively positive” for these utility names. Guggenheim adds FSLR may have helped shape key parts of the legislation—calling them “subsidy junkies” that know how to get what they want.

text: CHINA’S HUAWEI-LINKED SICARRIER DEVELOPS ALTERNATIVES TO $ASML TOOLS – NIKKEI A Chinese chip equipment firm tied to Huawei, SiCarrier Technologies, is quietly working to replace key tools from ASML, Applied Materials, and Lam Research, aiming to close one of China’s biggest tech gaps caused by U.S. export controls, according to Nikkei Asia. Backed by the Shenzhen government, SiCarrier is building tools across nearly every major chipmaking process and claims to have developed lithography machines for 28nm chips, though commercial viability remains unproven. The company has been hiring aggressively, especially as U.S. firms have scaled back operations in China, and is closely aligned with Huawei’s push to localize chip production and equipment. As the U.S., Netherlands, and Japan tighten export rules, China’s response is scaling fast—though catching up remains a long-term challenge.

text: In what world is Palantir similar to $GME and $AMC? If your argument is hype — then why would you compare the hype of Palantir to the hype of those two names? I would imagine you think Palantir is a real company unlike $GME. Yes retail gave Palantir attention but thats when the stock was at $6. Any retail person who gave it attention was smart. From $29.5 (last price before $SPY inclusion) —> $80 has not been because of retail hype. It’s been Wall St buying into a growth story, paying a very hefty premium (no disagreement there) but retail has not been buying Palantir at $70. Most of retail tbh has been selling parts of their position in this range. I get that earnings haven’t been $NVDA level, but they aren’t something to scoff at, and Q4 will either live up to more growth or it won’t. If it doesn’t and we see a dip, the question becomes how bad. I don’t see a 50% retracement but if it does get there, no one that I know who is a Palantir bull would be afraid of buying. Most people know its extended (and so does the street) but they continue to buy due to Palantir being one of the only real software AI names which eventually will reflect in earnings and is the reason why institutions have jumped in.
